$comment: zheref/bankai-handbooks' workflow policy, the policy half of the two-file model documented in zheref/hatsu docs/WORKFLOW.md: nen/contract.json says what nen EXECUTES (the canon lane and its verbs), this file says what the workflow DECIDES with. Hand-authored at the Hatsu adoption of 2026-10-20 (hatsu:tenkai), modelled on the canon sibling zheref/hatsu's own file: the blocks every skill reads the same way (models, notifications, profile, monitor, commits, reports.sections, futon) are carried verbatim from it; the blocks that are this repository's own (iteration, tests, coverage, review.scopes, release.unitPaths, direct, aiReviewers) are written for a prose repository. nen schema check validates this file at the pinned build; every value is a policy default, never a fact about the machine. The merge gate is G4 (CON-7): this is a canon repository, so every PR here ends at the maintainer's merge prompt and nothing merges it.

branch.$comment: The same shape nen/gates.json's delivery.head_ref_prefixes already admits (opus/, fable/, sonnet/, codex/): {model} is the model alias the actor runs on, {persona} the roster persona, {descriptor} a short kebab noun phrase. Supersedes the <persona>/<slug> form .claude/rules/04-commits-and-prs.md carried before the adoption.

iteration.$comment: The one declared check, run three times for three questions: breath proves it on the fresh tip, rasengan runs it while authoring, kokusen refuses a red tree before every commit. `lint` is scripts/canon_check.sh all (redaction, links, taxonomy), through hatsu:gyo. There is no build and no test suite here.

tests.$comment: No test suite exists (nen/contract.json's `test` seat says why), so kotoamatsukami has nothing to run and says so. An empty `required` is a statement, not an omission.

coverage.$comment: Prose has no line coverage; byakugan reports `not measurable here` against this ladder. It ships because every consumer that declares none inherits it.

launch.$comment: Nothing runs here; amaterasu launches nothing.

deploy.$comment: Canon is pulled by consumers through nen canon pin, never sent; nen/contract.json declares no target.

reports.$comment: `dir` is git-ignored. Only the final readiness report at the G4 gate is kept under it; turn and landing reports are published to the conversation.

sections.$comment: Maintainer's ruling of 2026-09-19 (zheref/hatsu#89): which blocks each report variant renders is configuration, read by nen report render --variant (v0.12.0), which injects sections.<block> presence flags for the template; every value inside a block is model-written. turn and landing are Spiritual Message (templates/spiritual-message.html); turn-fast is the per-turn publish under the fast profile (desk and last turn only); final and register are Rikugan (templates/rikugan.html; each has a .md twin filled from the same document) -- the dated final report is a one-effort Rikugan with a cleared desk, and register is what backlog-board, futon and backlog-loop render.

review.$comment: nen review scopes --base <ref> classifies a branch diff by these rows and hatsu:hanten raises each raised scope's persona within budget (reviews per effort, never per session). code is Nobunaga's and claims every path, deep because this is a process repository; architecture is Chrollo's -- the handbooks, the constitution and the conventions are exactly the architecture canon he cites, and he reviews them without ever authoring them (ROSTER ruling of 2026-09-09); security is Feitan's over the workflow, the scripts and the dependency contract; release is Phinks' over the release unit. ui, performance, surfaces and economics raise nothing in a prose repository and are not declared.

code.$comment: Every path: the conventions, the counts agreeing with their lists, the INDEX and stack-matrix rows agreeing with the files on disk, the CHANGELOG fragment and the PR body sections.

architecture.$comment: The canon itself: a stack rule refining its UZF parent and naming it, never contradicting it (AGENTS.md section 2 rule 6); a ports ruling citing both stacks' rule ids.

security.$comment: The CI workflow, the lint and release scripts, the nen dependency pin and digests, and the redaction policy a public tree depends on.

release.$comment: The release unit: the collated changelog, its fragments, the handbook set version every consumer pins, and the publisher mugetsu runs at G3.

mukai.$comment: Mukai starts En on the PR it opened in the same turn, as on the canon sibling.

release.$comment: What a release-proposal PR may touch beyond the collation: the fragments it consumes, the changelog it writes, and the handbook set version the tag carries.

direct.$comment: This repository declares no model/ label family in nen/labels.json, so hatsu:direct reports its picks and publishes nothing; opting in is a later PR that declares the family first (zheref/hatsu#240).

$comment:aiReviewers: Per-consumer AI reviewer expectation (zheref/hatsu#245): nen/gates.json names Copilot as the sole automated reviewer and round_policy owes one round; `optional` means a round is requested and counted where it lands and a Copilot request that never registers does not hold the PR off its G4 merge prompt -- the canon sibling's own value, taken on the same reasoning.

notifications.$comment: jutaisho's ladder, innermost first: `push` is the surface's own turn-complete signal, `os` an osascript notification, `sound` /System/Library/Sounds/<sound>.aiff through afplay. hooks/stop-bell.sh rings rungs 2 and 3 off .nen/last-stop.json; a rung absent from this list is not rung. `turn` decides how loud an ORDINARY turn is -- one with no gate: `rung1` (the default, and what an absent key reads as) rings only the first rung `rungs` lists, `all` rings every rung it lists. A GATE always rings everything `rungs` lists regardless of `turn`, and `turn` can only WITHHOLD an escalation `rungs` already grants -- it can never conjure a rung `rungs` does not list. nen reads and validates this key from v0.5.0 -- a closed set of `rung1` and `all`, refused by pointer on anything else -- and fires none of the three rungs itself; hooks/stop-bell.sh is what rings them.

commits.$comment: Prospective commits carry exactly the canonical persona trailer that truthfully identifies the actor: Hatsu-Agent for Hatsu work (Kurapika here), Akatsuki-Agent for the CI plane. No model, surface, runtime, session or generated-credit attribution anywhere (CON-51(c), BC-7); .claude/rules/04-commits-and-prs.md says the same in prose. nen commit format --repo reads this list.

monitor.$comment: en's izanagi cap and its poll interval. The cap is grammar, not a default: a watch loop with no cap does not run.

profile.$comment: The run profile hatsu:ren reads (zheref/hatsu#93). `default` applies to every turn that names none; a turn may name one with --profile or the words "fast turn" / "thorough turn", and only a value in `allowed` is accepted. fast: steps 1 to 3 per turn, a turn-fast page, the launch skipped for the turn (not moved: mukai has no launch step), the full page and coverage deferred to mukai; standard: today's turn; thorough: the impacted suites (kotoamatsukami) on every turn. A landing (mukai) always runs thorough. Validated by nen schema check from v0.13.0; an older pin preserves the key as raw data.

models.rule: latest alias only, never a version; subagents never on the frontier tier

cursor.note: Cursor-native only; provider models there are reserved for Bugbot

antigravity.note: Google AI / Gemini tiers. A persona's model accepts only inherit, flash or pro (https://antigravity.google/docs/subagents, fetched 2026-09-20), so economy maps to flash here; flash_lite is not a documented persona value

roles.$comment: watcher and formatter run on economy (zheref/hatsu#93): Illumi and hatsu:izanami polls run as watcher, formatting passes (gyo's auto-fix, prose reflow) as formatter. A role maps to a tier, never to a model. A subagent's tier is its scope's or role's, never its caller's (zheref/hatsu#222, ruling of 2026-10-13): a reviewer keeps its scope's declared tier (review.scopes.<scope>.tier, this reviewer tier by default) when hatsu:direct sends the maintainer's own session to fast or economy; docs/WORKFLOW.md section models states it.

models.$comment: A tier is named, never a model version — a pinned version is a pin that rots. The orchestrator tier is the main session's; a SUBAGENT never runs on it, because the frontier tier is where the human's own conversation lives. Below it a subagent's tier is its role's, never its caller's (roles.$comment, zheref/hatsu#222).

futon.$comment: The ADVANCE-GO GATE -- the maintainer's rulings of 2026-09-26 and 2026-09-28 (docs/ROSTER.md § Rulings of 2026-09-26/27/28: getsuga and kagutsuchi take an advance go on any repository kind; mugetsu only on a process or library repository, never a product that deploys or uploads to a store; the three kinds are docs/WORKFLOW.md § Repository kinds). `nen parse futon` annotates every skill-chain step whose skill is listed here with gate: {allowed, kind, reason}, the kind being `nen repo classify`'s own verdict for the resolved repo (unknown fails closed); a skill not listed here gets no gate, and futon § 8 refuses a listed skill's step that carries none. From nen v0.15.1 an ABSENT key falls back to nen's built-in default policy (gate.source "default"), and a declared one replaces it wholesale (gate.source "declared") -- hatsu declares its own so the policy is read from here. The policy lives here and nowhere in prose: mugetsu § 3 and futon § 8 read the gate line verbatim.
